newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore economy grows 7.8 pct in second quarter.
newsitem.headline: Singapore economy grows 7.8 pct in second quarter.

text.p: The Singapore economy picked up significantly in the second quarter, expanding by 7.8 percent on year and against 4.1 percent against the prior quarter, the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) said on Tuesday.
Economic growth for the first half year was pegged at 5.9 percent, the ministry said in a statement.
Except for business services, all sectors registered faster growth, with manufacturing showing the most significant pick up.
Manufacturing output grew by 3.2 percent year-on-year in the second quarter after three consecutive quarters of decline.
The financial and business sector grew by 10.6 percent in the April-June period from the year before, against 10.7 percent in the first quarter, it said.
In the financial services sub-sector, foreign exchange and Asian currency loans growth remained robust, but credit growth in commercial banks continued to moderate, it said.
Growth of the business services sub-sector moderated to 7.1 percent, MTI said.
A jump in entrepot trade growth to 15 percent in the second quarter helped push commerce sector growth to 7.9 percent, up from 2.8 percent a quarter earlier.
"Growth in entrepot trade was driven largely by re-exports of electronics products to two of our largest markets, Malaysia and the U.S.," it added.
The transport and communications sector expanded by 9.5 percent, up from eight percent a quarter ago.
The ministry said the communications sector continued to expand strongly and that liberalisation of the market since April had stimulated mobile communications demand.
The construction industry grew by 11.8 percent, up from 10 percent a quarter earlier.
Growth was supported largely by public-sector building and upgrading activities and infrastructural projects, it said.
MTI said investment commitments were also positive with the manufacturing sector attracting Singapore $2.5 billion in the second quarter.
The United States and Japan remained the largest investors, committing $789 million and $672 million respectively.
It said the business community was "generally optimistic" about business activity in the next six month up to December.
But the extent of optimism varied from industry to industry with some like electronics, experiencing "uneven growth", an MTI official told reporters.
He said the chemical and marine industries, for example, were facing keen competition.
Meanwhile, exchange rate uncertainties within the region might also have some negative impact on the economy, he said.
The Singapore dollar has depreciated about five percent against the U.S. unit since the beginning of the year.

Effects on the economy remain to be seen but are unlikely to have a clear-cut, one-directional impact on trade or inflation, said an official of the Monetary Authority of Singapore, the de facto central bank.
